title: Existence of a canonical colouring for colourable graphs
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph and let $k$ be a natural number. If $G$ is $k$-colourable, then $G$ admits a canonical colouring consisting of at most $k$ colour classes; that is, there is a list $(V_1, V_2, \dots, V_m)$ of pairwise disjoint sets of vertices with $m \le k$, whose union is the whole vertex set, in which each $V_i$ is a maximal independent set of $G$ among the vertices left uncoloured by $V_1, \dots, V_{i-1}$.
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite simple graph
replaced:
\emph{Show that if \texttt{G} is
\texttt{k}-vertex-colourable, then \texttt{G} has a canonical \texttt{k}-vertex colouring.}
